audit.whatIsWrong: Nimbus Strike is called 'his only gap-close — he cannot reach you while it is down' in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t, and the whole green-light system is built on that claim.
audit.why: Wukong has two dashes. Riot's text for Warrior Trickster: 'Wukong becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone that will attack nearby enemies' — 22/21/20/19/18 seconds. So the page's central instruction, step up whenever Nimbus Strike is down, walks a champion with no escape until 6 into a second dash he was told did not exist. And the invisibility is missed entirely: the page treats Warrior Trickster as a decoy that baits your shield, when the actual danger is that Wukong himself vanishes and repositions while you are looking at the clone.
audit.corrected: Nimbus Strike (10s at rank 1, 650 range, needs a target) is not his only dash. Warrior Trickster is a second one on 22s, and it turns him invisible while it leaves the clone behind.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (W description, cooldown 22/21/20/19/18; E cooldown 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7, range 650)

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone is credited with eating Wukong's damage in five places — 'Void Stone's 15% reduction eats a chunk of his AD burst', 'Void Stone eats his AD burst', 'Void Stone's 15% magic reduction blanks his clone-and-spin all-in'.
audit.why: Void Stone reduces magic damage taken. Wukong's damage is physical throughout — Crushing Blow is an empowered attack that shreds armour, Nimbus Strike and Cyclone are physical, and Stone Skin is armour and regeneration. The page is crediting the passive with reducing exactly the damage type it does not touch, and it does so in the sentences that tell you when the all-in stops killing you. The honest version is better advice anyway: what saves you at the first item is Catalyst/Rod of Ages health, not the passive, and the reason you win the late game is that HIS armour is the dead stat, not yours.
audit.corrected: Void Stone is dead weight in this lane — every point Wukong deals is physical. Catalyst and Rod of Ages health is what blunts the all-in; his stacked armour is the stat that goes to waste, not yours.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Q armour shred, P armour and regeneration)

audit.whatIsWrong: Cyclone is named four times as the one thing that catches you, and its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: It is 130/110/90 seconds at 315 range. That is the longest cooldown on either side of this matchup and it is the single cleanest green light the page could give a Kassadin: once Cyclone is spent, the only tool that can pin a blinking assassin is gone for over two minutes at rank 1. Naming the ability as the threat without the number leaves the reader permanently afraid of it instead of counting it.
audit.corrected: Cyclone: 130s at rank 1, 315 range. Spent Cyclone is a two-minute window in which nothing in his kit stops a Riftwalk chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Crushing Blow is described as an armour shred but never as an auto-attack reset, so the page gives you no tell to read.
audit.why: Riot's text is 'Wukong's next attack gains attack range, deals bonus damage, and reduces the target's armor' — it carries the auto-reset flag, which is the flagged interaction for this matchup. Two things follow. The burst arrives on the attack wind-up rather than on a visible cast, so 'he E's in, lands the Q' actually reads as one motion. And it GAINS attack range, stepping from 250 at rank 1 up to 350 at rank 5, so the safe distance you learned at level 2 is wrong by level 9.
audit.corrected: Crushing Blow is an 8s auto-attack reset whose range grows from 250 to 350 as he ranks it. Read the wind-up, and recheck your spacing as it levels.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Q description, cooldown 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, range 250/275/300/325/350, autoReset flag)

audit.why: Sides and ratings untouched. Wukong owning 1-3 and the item stages with Skill at 6 is consistent with a champion who has two dashes and an armour-stacking passive against a champion with one blink, and the 50.00% over 34 games is genuinely even — there is no directional evidence to move a cell.
Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield. It has never silenced in this kit version, and silence is a category the kit builder tracks, so its absence is meaningful.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.why: 50.00% over 34 games. The page quotes no figure. No change.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are flatly his. Wukong's Q (Crushing Blow) shreds your armor for bonus damage, and his E dash means he chooses every trade while you have only Null Sphere and its 1.5s shield. Do not step up to throw a Q for poke — he just E's in, lands the armor-shred Q, and runs you down. Lean on Nether Blade to keep mana up, farm at max range, eat the chip, and respect that his W clone exists purely to bait your shield or your flash.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are flatly his. Crushing Blow (8s) is an auto-attack reset that shreds your armour, so the wind-up is the tell rather than any cast, and Nimbus Strike (10s, 650 range) lets him pick every trade while you hold only Null Sphere. Do not step up to poke — he dashes in, resets the armour-shred, and runs you down. Farm at max range on Nether Blade mana, and respect that Warrior Trickster turns him invisible as well as leaving the clone.

edits.before: This is your stabilization window, not a fight window. Nether Blade's mana restore and a maxed Null Sphere let you farm and weather his Q-and-E pokes. At 6, Riftwalk is the equalizer — but use it to blink away from his E gap-close or out of his R (Cyclone) knockup, not to brawl, because he still out-stats you pre-items. Bait the W clone first; if you blink onto the decoy you have nothing left when the real Wukong commits with his real R.
edits.after: This is your stabilization window, not a fight window. Nether Blade's mana restore and a maxed Null Sphere let you farm and weather his Q-and-E poke. At 6, Riftwalk is the equalizer — spend it leaving Nimbus Strike or Cyclone's knockup, not brawling, because he still out-stats you pre-items. Cyclone is 130s at rank 1, so a spent one is a long pass. Bait Warrior Trickster first: it cloaks him as well as cloning him, so a blink at the decoy leaves you empty.

edits.before: This is where it tips your way. Wukong builds armor and bruiser HP to win brawls, but your damage is entirely magic — Void Stone's 15% reduction eats a chunk of his AD burst and his stacked armor does nothing to stop you. With Riftwalk ramping and your AP online, blink-spam lets you assassinate squishies and re-blink out before his R (Cyclone) can knock you up, the one tool that actually catches you. He is item-dependent and even-curved; you scale past him — just make sure you survived his lane to get here.
edits.after: This is where it tips your way. Wukong builds armour and bruiser HP to win brawls, but your damage is entirely magic, so his stacked armour is the dead stat — Void Stone is dead weight the other way, since every point he deals is physical. With Riftwalk ramping and your AP online, blink-spam assassinates squishies and re-blinks out before Cyclone (130s at rank 1) can knock you up, the one tool that catches you. He is item-dependent and even-curved; you scale past him.

edits.after: Riftwalk lets you leave Nimbus Strike and Cyclone's knockup, though Void Stone is dead weight against an all-physical Wukong — it stays even.

edits.after: Catalyst/Rod health is what stops his clone-and-spin all-in one-shotting you, since his damage is physical, and ramping Riftwalk turns the corner.

notes: Two errors here pointed in opposite directions and both were load-bearing. 'Nimbus Strike is his only gap-close' underwrites the entire green-light system on the page while Warrior Trickster is a second dash that also grants invisibility. And Void Stone was credited with eating Wukong's damage in five strings when every point of it is physical — the same passive is correctly called dead weight on the Tryndamere page, so the repo is inconsistent with itself about what Void Stone does. A cheap check worth running: for every Kassadin matchup, compare whether the page claims Void Stone value against an enemy whose kit carries no magic damage.
